# Diagnosis — Isolating the Part Behind a Periodic RA Spike

**Dimension:** tools and procedures to confirm a mechanical periodic spike, measure its
period accurately, and isolate the component; plus non-mount causes to rule out. Sources:
[citations.md](../citations.md).

## Tools

| Tool | Relevant capability | Source |
|---|---|---|
| PHD2 Guiding Assistant | Measure mount behaviour with guiding disabled, "at least as long as the worm period" | [33] |
| PHD2 Log Viewer | "Identify RA drive harmonics by looking at the RA frequency analysis"; FFT window/resolution undocumented | [35] |
| EQMOD PECPrep | Filters "wind, seeing effects, linear and non linear drift" [37]; period slider to "isolate other periodic signals"; phase column groups components "from the same mechanical source"; resolution slider; saved reference spectrum for before/after | [36] |
| OpenAstro Guide Insight | Periodogram export as CSV | [39] |

## Measurement accuracy

- **FFT bin quantisation shifts reported periods.** PECPrep: "the 470 second peak listed
  will actually correspond to the 479s worm period" [36]. Resolution trades bin width
  against short-period range [36].
- **A sharp spike may appear only as a harmonic series.** John Sim found no peak at ~110 s
  but peaks at 54.6, 36.4, 27.3, 21.8, 18.1, 15.6, 13.6 s, "nearly an exact harmonic of
  109.2 seconds" [17]; Andy Galasso read the same log as ~120 s [17].
- **Guiding can distort the apparent period.** OzAndrewJ: "the 133 seconds may be affected
  by the act of guiding. If you run an unguided test, and the period becomes 122 seconds
  then its more than likely … the pulley on the motor" [15].
- **Odd-harmonic dominance** "might indicate that the associated mechanical part is being
  restricted in its movement" [36].

Implication (inference): a 134–138 s spread from Log Viewer FFT may partly be bin and
guiding effects. An unguided capture analysed in PECPrep with the period slider set to the
candidate period is the cited way to pin it down [36][38].

## Procedure (each step cited)

1. **Baseline profile.** New profile; guide speed 0.5–1x; mount backlash compensation off;
   2 s exposures on a star near Dec 0 [34]. RA backlash is "irrelevant to guiding" [19].
2. **Rule out the payload.** Loop exposures and gently push the guide scope / tug cables
   [33]; "a movement of only 5 microns can create an apparent tracking error … of over 6
   arc-sec" [34].
3. **Unguided capture.** Calibrate, then restart PHD2 with "Enable Mount Guide Output"
   unchecked; 1–2 s exposures for ~45–50 min [38]; capture "at least 5 times the worm
   period … For an EQ6 this 40 mins" with guiding off, star near Dec 0, no meridian crossing
   [36].
4. **Time-domain check.** Did the big move start with a large guide command (software) or is
   it followed by corrections (mechanical)? [33]
5. **Frequency check.** Log Viewer RA frequency analysis [35]; look for a harmonic family,
   not only a single peak [17].
6. **PECPrep isolation.** Load the unguided log; AutoFilter; set the stacked-cycle period to
   the candidate (e.g. 136 s) and see whether spikes stack; use the phase column; save a
   reference spectrum [36].
7. **Compare against candidate component periods** — see
   [drivetrain-periods.md](drivetrain-periods.md): motor pulley 119.7 s, belt tooth 9.97 s,
   worm 478.7 s, 608 worm-bearing 2 × BSF 136.2–142.3 s, BPFI 107.7–110.4 s (all est.).
8. **Physical confirmation.** Remove the RA belt cover and watch the drive for ≥2 minutes
   through a spike [17]; listen for a tone change during slow slews [28].
9. **Change one part at a time and re-measure** against the saved reference [36][38].
   Dan Watt's sequence (belt → spur gears → pulley → motor → worm bearings) is a worked
   example; the last step fixed it [15].

## Counter-perspective: non-mount causes

- PHD2 manual: most large abrupt deflections "arise from neither the mount nor PHD2's guide
  commands", mostly from the guide scope/camera assembly [34]. For RA, "unusually large,
  randomly space[d] deflections are more likely to arise from the sorts of mechanical
  problems described here than from errors in the RA drive system" [34].
  - Limit: this addresses *randomly spaced* deflections. A spike on a fixed period is not
    random, which (inference) points back toward a rotating part.
- Cables bind "in certain sky positions or after a meridian flip" [34] — position-dependent,
  not fixed-period (inference).
- Waddington ranked guide-scope and cable causes ahead of RA-drive grit for an EQ6-R with
  1–2 minute spikes [19]; the owner confirmed the spikes in unguided 5 s frames, establishing
  a mount event [19].
- Short-period motor-stage faults are not guidable: an 11 s pinion-gear wobble on an AVX "requires a mechanical fix" [32].
- PE testing names a period, not a part: "That cannot be determined from the PE testing" —
  swap parts and re-measure [38].

## Gaps and limitations

- PHD2 Log Viewer's FFT window, bin width and raw-RA reconstruction are not documented in the
  fetched pages [35].
- No source quantifies how far guiding shifts an apparent period.
- A "both axes drop together" USB/power signature appeared only in an unreadable page and is
  not cited.
